newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Gas Oil/Jet - Diesel attempts slight rebound.
newsitem.headline: Asia Gas Oil/Jet - Diesel attempts slight rebound.

text.p: Singapore gas oil market made a meek attempt at a recovery on Tuesday as prices for second-half June climbed back up over $25.00 per barrel, but prompt cargoes remained soft amid abundant offers, traders said.

Traders said three 150,000-barrel cargoes were traded at $25.10 per barrel for June 22-26 liftings, on a free-on-board (fob) basis, sustained by several bids at that level, but most sellers were focused on June 11-15 at $24.90.
A Singapore trader bought from a German trader at $25.10, while a Japanese trader bought two cargoes--at $25.10 from a European refiner and at $25.00 from a Mediterranean trader.
The group of three buyers had altogether bought nearly 22 million barrels since March 3.
Traders said the contango was also seen on the swaps market with July quoted at $24.85/$24.95 per barrel, five cents more than June.
"The contango could be even sharper in the further months as there is a lot of talk of pressure to cut (refinery) runs," one trader said.

Industry sources said Esso Singapore has cut crude runs at its 230,000-barrel-per-day (bpd) refinery by 10 percent due to negative profit margins. Shell said it was monitoring the margins daily and would cut runs if losses worsened.
They said the market remained well-supplied with sellers offering 10 cargoes and noted that the near term outlook remained bearish as China were uninterested to sell amid high stocks in the country.

China's recent lack of appetite was reflected by the low volumes of diesel it imported in April at around 371,000 tonnes, compared with about 740,000 tonnes in March, according to official customs figures.
Traders said that at its current rate of imports and amid the continued congestion at the southern port of Xiamen, China could import an even smaller volume in May compared with April.

Sri Lanka is contemplating issuing another tender to buy gas oil and jet fuel for June on top of the tender which closes on Wednesday, ahead of the unscheduled shutdown at its 55,000-bpd refinery during the first week of June.
Jet fuel was well-offered at higher levels with four cargoes seen between $24.35 and $24.60 per barrel fob, for mid-June liftings, but buyers were at bay.
